title: Terrain Tiles: global elevation of land and sea floor in Web Mercator tiles to zoom 15, compiled from SRTM, EU-DEM, 3DEP, ETOPO1 and others
provider: Mapzen (Linux Foundation), on the AWS Open Data registry (s3://elevation-tiles-prod)
credit: Elevation: Mapzen Terrain Tiles (SRTM, EU-DEM, 3DEP, ETOPO1 and others)
format: PNG tiles of 256 x 256 pixels in Web Mercator (EPSG:3857), zooms 0 to 15; elevation in metres above mean sea level = R x 256 + G + B / 256 - 32768 (the Terrarium encoding). Each tile names its source datasets in the HTTP header x-amz-meta-x-imagery-sources (for example srtm/N45E006.hgt, eudem/eudem_dem_5deg_n45e005.tif, etopo1/ETOPO1_Bed_g.tif). Read by the data library's tile service (data/tiles), which fetches the tiles a terrain tile needs on demand, keeps them in data/cache/aws-terrain-tiles/terrarium/<z>/<x>/<y>.png with their sources, and records each tile's sources and the resolution behind each sample.
coverage: Global between 85.05 S and 85.05 N (Web Mercator); land at 3 to 90 m (SRTM 30 m between 60 N and 56 S; EU-DEM 25 m in Europe; 3DEP 10 m in the United States; ArcticDEM, CDEM, LINZ and others), the sea floor at ETOPO1's 1 arc-minute (about 1.85 km), GMTED's 250 m to 1 km elsewhere.
licence: Mixed; attribution required. The data sources and the attribution each requires are listed at https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/attribution.md; among them SRTM, 3DEP, ETOPO1 and GMTED are US Government works in the public domain, EU-DEM is 'Produced using Copernicus data and information funded by the European Union - EU-DEM layers', CDEM is under the Open Government Licence - Canada, and LINZ under CC BY 4.0. The page names the sources of what it shows.
citation: Mapzen, Terrain Tiles, https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/ (tiles retrieved on demand; each tile's retrieval is recorded beside it).
